planner.question: Can a nonlocal difference representation preserve all NAE solutions and permit efficient global gluing?
planner.strategy: Exact cut-space recoding with fundamental cycle equations.
planner.alternative: Fixed-parameter syndrome DP exploiting nonbridge degree structure.
planner.stop_rule: Stop on unsupported universal cost or coverage; redirect away from representation-only optimization after mixed hardness.
literature_leads: Prior section obstruction and mixed typed solver; standard 3SAT NP-completeness, reduction derived in note.

construct.claim: NAE triples admit exact global difference representation by homogeneous cycle equations and positive incident-edge OR clauses.
construct.scope: Monotone distinct-variable NAE triples, one pivot each, simple graph.
construct.derivation: Take XOR edge differences; characterize image by fundamental cycles; lift via forest paths; characterize typing by bridge incidences.
unresolved_steps: Universal tractable global compatibility and general SAT coverage.
candidate_tests: All four-variable pivot configurations and five-variable triple subsets; verify cut image, lift and exact typing boundary.

alternative.claim: The graph-derived mixed system admits exact 2^O(r) polynomial-time-factor completion parameterized by cycle rank.
alternative.scope: Positive incident-edge binary clauses on graph edge differences; no general bounded rank assumption.
alternative.derivation: Fix bridges to one; enumerate high-degree incident edge bits; remaining OR graph has degree at most two; dynamic program with syndrome and combine by XOR.
unresolved_steps: Uniform logarithmic cycle rank or a different universally efficient completion.
candidate_tests: Actual DP against exhaustive source models, disjoint triples, long even and odd cycles.

objections: Unrestricted mixed cycle/OR compatibility is NP-complete.
Exact recoding is not a universal typability guarantee.
counterexample_candidates: All triples on five vertices; explicit 3SAT to monotone NAE reduction.
critic.equivalence_audit: Fundamental-cycle orthogonality is necessary and sufficient; bridge pinning is existence-preserving, not all-model preserving.
critic.barrier_audit: NP-completeness of mixed representation does not prove P!=NP; no optimal pivot claim.
